stops.title: Milestone two at a glance
stops.text: This video explains milestone two of W S version six, at its merge gate. In this milestone, a Rust daemon called W S D replaces the Z shell version of W S on one machine. The graph shows the outcome in the middle, and around it the changes, the delivered phases, the deviations, the setbacks, the review, the hand test and the rollback.

Here is the outcome. The W S command now runs on one Rust daemon instead of shell scripts and lock files. The daemon owns sessions, logs, messages, dependency edges, triggers and a local MCP server. The command names, the flags, the output and the exit codes stay the same. To go back, one command switches to the Z shell backend.

stops.title: The changes
stops.text: The changes share one idea: one process owns all state. Each session has an append-only log with a hash chain. A SQLite registry is a projection that the daemon can rebuild from those logs. Sessions survive a closed terminal and a daemon restart. Messages are log events with confirmed delivery. Each change links to the phases that built it.

stops.title: Done when checks
stops.text: Thirty-five of thirty-six Done when checks are met. The met rows cover the log, the registry, sessions, messages, triggers, the importer, MCP, Loop runners and the installer.

stops.title: The partial check
stops.text: Look at the one that is partial. Phase thirty-eight asks for a non-blocking review verdict and a hand check before the merge. The review is a comment, which does not block. The hand check is still yours to do.

stops.title: Three deviations
stops.text: Three things differ from the plan. First, the plan put the install before the dry run of the import. But the install starts the daemon, and the daemon imports at its first start. So the dry run must come first. Second, the latency test of the hook ingest now runs only when you set a flag, because it failed at random under load. Third, a new phase, seventy-one, joins milestone three to fix finding F4.

stops.title: Phase twenty-one
stops.text: Now the setbacks, the costs on the way. Phase twenty-one cost the most. Its tests failed at random while other loops loaded the machine, so the orchestrator asked a human. The fix made the tests wait for an event instead of a clock, and then twenty full Verify runs passed.

stops.title: The other setbacks
stops.text: The milestone took forty-four attempts for thirty-six phases, with nine retries, two model escalations, three questions and one human-in-the-loop pause, in about twenty hours. Phase thirteen needed a stronger model to fix a lock file race. A Codex usage limit cost two attempts in phase twenty-eight.

stops.title: The review
stops.text: The review used the max tier of Adversarial Review, with two outer rounds. The final Opus review posted a comment, so nothing blocks the merge. One major finding is deferred. W S new with an agent can fail under load, because tmux cannot find the new window. Run the command again. Phase seventy-one fixes it in milestone three. Six minor findings stay open.

stops.title: Dry run before the install
stops.text: Before you merge, test it by hand. The order matters. Build the release binary and run the import as a dry run first. Then install. The install starts the daemon, and the daemon imports at once, so a later dry run only shows the stored plan.

stops.title: The hand test
stops.text: After the install, check that the daemon runs and that the import is complete. Then send a message, drive W S from an agent through MCP, run a handoff with a trigger, and restart the daemon under a headless session. Last, merge the pull request, update your dotfile folder, and resume the Loop. Each step links to the phases that it checks.

stops.title: Rollback
stops.text: If something goes wrong, roll back in three steps. First, switch W S back to the Z shell backend while the daemon still runs. Then stop the daemon with launchctl. To return to Rust later, install again first, then select the Rust backend.

stops.title: Explore the milestone
stops.text: That is milestone two of W S version six. The page has every Done when row, every finding and every hand-test command with its code reference. Open the page before you merge the pull request.
